 Judgment

MFA No.200101/2019 is filed by the claimant seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VII at Vijayapur (for short 'Tribunal') in MVC No.289/2015, vide its judgment and award dated 23.10.2018 while MFA No.200334/2019 is filed by the insurer challenging the liability fastened on it to pay the compensation awarded in the above case.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT-VII at Vijayapur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It also challenged the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal.
The records disclose that the claimant suffered injuries in a road traffic accident on 03.11.2014 at about 1.30 a.m. when he was riding pillion on a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-28/W-4482.
The claimant claimed that the rider of the motorcycle was negligent and could not control it and the vehicle skidded.
As a result the claimant suffered fracture of left femur and other injuries.
The claimant was shifted to Vaibhav Hospital, Vijayapur, where he was treated as an inpatient for 15 days.
He was thereafter treated at Dr.Nayak Hospital, Vijayapur.
The claimant was a barber by profession and was earning Rs.15,000/- per month and due to the injuries, he was disabled to pursue his avocation.
Therefore, he filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.16,50,000/-.
3. The claim petition was resisted by the insurer who denied the accident and the injuries suffered by the claimant as well as entitlement of the claimant for NC: 2023:KHC-K:5554 compensation.
The insurer contended that there was a delay in lodging the complaint and that the rider did not possess a valid licence.
4. Based on these rival contentions, the claim petition was set down for trial.
The claimant was examined as PW.1 and he marked Exs.P1 to P13.
He also examined a doctor as PW.2 who deposed that the claimant had suffered fracture of left femur and that he had suffered disability to the extent of 35% to 40% to the left lower limb.

The insurer examined the record keeper at Vaibhav Hospital,
Vijayapur as RW.1 and one of its officials as RW.2 and marked Exs.R1 to R4.
5.
Based on the oral and documentary evidence, the Tribunal held that the accident was due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the motorcycle.

It also held that the claimant had suffered The Branch Manager vs Dunduraj And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65287927/
3 fracture of left femur for which he underwent a surgery.

sentences.text: The Tribunal noticed that fractures were not united and that the implants were in situ.

Therefore, the Tribunal assessed the disability NC:
2023:KHC-K:5554 suffered by the claimant at 10% to the whole body.

The Tribunal considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month and his age at 20 years and awarded the following compensation:

The Tribunal directed the owner and insurer of the motorcycle to pay the aforesaid compensation along with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of realisation.

7. Being aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant is in NC:
2023:KHC-K:5554 appeal while the insurer had challenged its liability to pay the compensation as well as rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal.

8. The learned counsel for the claimant contended that the claimant was a barber by profession and the material documents indicated that the fracture of left femur was malunited and therefore, the disability affected his profession and therefore, disability assessed was meager and warranted enhancement.
He further contended that the notional income of the claimant ought to have been considered at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month.
He also contended that the compensation awarded under the conventional heads deserve enhancement.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurer contended that though the accident happened on 03.11.2014, RW.1 who was the record keeper at Vaibhav Hospital, Vijayapur, deposed that the The Branch Manager vs Dunduraj And Anr on 19 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65287927/
4 claimant was admitted on 02.11.2014 at 4.00 p.m.

sentences.text: She further NC: 2023:KHC-K:5554 contended that Ex.R1 which was the case sheet at Vaibhav Hospital, Vijayapur indicated that the accident occurred on 02.11.2014 and hence, contended that the medical records were concocted by the claimant to launch a false claim.
She further contended that the Tribunal without any basis had awarded interest at the rate of 9% per annum.
10. I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the claimant and the learned counsel for the insurer.
11. The fact that the claimant suffered fracture of left femur is evident from Exs.P4, P8, P11 and P13.

The contention of the insurer that the claimant was admitted at hospital on 02.11.2014 and therefore, the medical records are concocted is liable to be rejected outrightly since there was a overwriting in Ex.R1 whereby the date is shown as 02.11.2014 by overwriting the date '3' as '2'.
The person who had overwritten this date was obviously the record keeper or some one else in the hospital.
The NC: 2023:KHC-K:5554 said documents such as complaint at Ex.P2 and FIR at Ex.P1 all indicate that the accident happened on 03.11.2014.
Therefore, the finding of the Tribunal that the rider of the motorcycle had caused accident on 03.11.2014 does not warrant any interference.

12. In so far as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the claimant was a barber by profession and as rightly contended by the learned counsel for the claimant, the fracture of the left femur was malunited and this must have resulted in some amount of disability and discomfort.

Having regard to the fact that the malunited fracture affected the day to day activities of the claimant, this Court considers it appropriate to assess the disability suffered by the claimant at 12%
to the whole body.
Likewise, the Tribunal must have been considered the notional income of the claimant at a sum of Rs.7,500/- per month.
The Tribunal failed to award any compensation towards loss of income during the period of - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5554 treatment.
Consequently, the claimant is entitled to enhanced compensation which is re-determined as follows:

sentences.text: 13 . In view of the above, the appeal filed by the claimant in MFA No.200101/2019 and the appeal filed by the insurer in MFA No.200334/2019 are allowed in part.

The compensation of Rs.2,83,800/- awarded by the Tribunal is enhanced to a sum of Rs.3,81,100/- which is payable by the insurer along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum instead of 9% per annum awarded by the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC-K:5554 Tribunal, from the date of claim petition till the date of realization.
The enhanced compensation amount along with interest shall be deposited by the insurer before the Tribunal within a period of one month from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this Judgment.
Upon deposit, 50% of the enhanced compensation and interest shall be deposited in the name of the claimant in any nationalized Bank for a period of three years.
The amount in deposit in MFA No.200334/2019 is ordered to be transmitted to the Tribunal for necessary orders.
Learned counsel Smt.Preeti Patil Melkundi is permitted to file vakalath for respondent No.2/insurer in MFA No.200101/2019 within two weeks from today.
